title: Шеф в больничной палате  (The Chef in the Hospital Ward)

segments.t: After Max and Kostya leave for the restaurant hoping Sasha and Nastya will cool off during their shift, the scene shifts to the hospital ward. There, Chef Barinov impatiently questions his doctor about his MRI results and chafes against the strict hospital regimen.
А не нужно квартире устраивать, ты рано!
Что, может мешаться?
Ну, на Пашку посмотри.
Придут на работу, обо всем договорятся.
Как самочувствие ваше?
Так это же я вас хотел спросить.
Как мое самочувствие?
Нет, нет, не волнуйтесь.
Дождемся результатов МРТ.
От вас требуется только одно.
Строго соблюдать режим.
Я сделаю все, что возможно.
Я надеюсь, вы скоро нас покинете.
Right, let's take their exchange slowly and unpack the Russian.
А не нужно квартире устраивать, ты рано!

'There is no need to make a scene in the apartment so early!' Max declares that there is no need to make a scene in the apartment so early as the tension in the room peaks. Russian packs the whole idea of what is allowed or needed into one impersonal word at the front.
Что, может мешаться?

'What, could it get in the way?' Wondering what it get in the way could is how Vika puts Max on the spot. In Russian, she does not need helper words like "do" or "did"—rising pitch alone turns it into a question.
Ну, на Пашку посмотри.
'Well, just take a look at Pashka.' Around the shift and kitchen, Max sets a calm, everyday tone with Vika.
Придут на работу, обо всем договорятся.
'They will get to work and sort everything out.' Vika mentions that they will get to work and sort everything out so Max sees what is at stake.
Как самочувствие ваше?

'How are you feeling today?' Wondering how Vika feeling today is cuts straight through the tension between Max and Vika. Even in the middle of the drama, he keeps the polite plural "you" that workplace Russian expects.
Так это же я вас хотел спросить.
'That is actually what I wanted to ask you.' Pointing out that that is actually what she wanted to ask Max gives Max a sobering reality check.
Как мое самочувствие?

'How am I feeling?' Over the conversation and the hope, Max presses Vika for a straight answer. In Russian, he does not need helper words like "do" or "did"—rising pitch alone turns it into a question.
Нет, нет, не волнуйтесь.
'No, no, do not worry.' Realizing that do not worry changes how Vika handles the situation.
Дождемся результатов МРТ.
'Let us wait for the MRI results.' Noting that they should wait for the results keeps Max's side of the story simple and clear.
От вас требуется только одно.

'Only one thing is required of you.' Even though only one thing is required of Max, Vika keeps a steady face in front of Max. Notice how she sticks to the formal "you", keeping a professional line between them.
Строго соблюдать режим.
'To follow the regimen strictly.' With the moment and hospital in play, Max keeps this short reply brisk and direct.
Я сделаю все, что возможно.
'I will do everything I possibly can.' Saying that she will do everything she possibly can is how Vika sets the tone with Max.
Я надеюсь, вы скоро нас покинете.

'I hope you will be leaving us very soon.' Claiming that he hopes Vika will be leaving them very soon sounds confident, even if Vika has doubts. Even in the middle of the drama, he keeps the polite plural "you" that workplace Russian expects. Now let's listen to the entire scene again without interruption.
А не нужно квартире устраивать, ты рано!
Что, может мешаться?
Ну, на Пашку посмотри.
Придут на работу, обо всем договорятся.
Как самочувствие ваше?
Так это же я вас хотел спросить.
Как мое самочувствие?
Нет, нет, не волнуйтесь.
Дождемся результатов МРТ.
От вас требуется только одно.
Строго соблюдать режим.
Я сделаю все, что возможно.
Я надеюсь, вы скоро нас покинете.

That wraps up this scene as max and Kostya hope the girls will make peace at work, while in the hospital Chef Barinov argues with his doctor about his MRI results and strict bed rest. See you next time!
До свидания!
